title: LinkedPhone pricing: Is it actually worth it?
summary: Is LinkedPhone pricing really simple and affordable? Here's what LinkedPhone costs for your small and growing business, now and in the future.
body_markdown:
LinkedPhone markets itself as a simple and affordable business phone option. But is it?


On the surface, it may seem like it. LinkedPhone pricing starts around $20 per month with one user included. But those plans are built for individual small businesses with one[business phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-business-phone-number/) . They’re not designed for scaling and fast-growing businesses.


For example, every extra user and phone number costs $5 per month. Some features, like “premium AI,” also have additional fees. A plan that costs $20 per month when you have a team of one can quickly grow to $300+ per month once you add users and numbers.


In this article, we’ll break down what you need to know about LinkedPhone’s pricing, including:


- Core features
- Limitations their sales page doesn’t mention
- Hidden fees and paid add-ons
- Alternatives that might be a better fit for your team and needs


**LinkedPhone** **pricing** **:** LinkedPhone


pricing


starts at $19.99 per month for one user at a local number. Toll-free numbers start at $29.99 per month. Additional users and/or numbers cost $5 more per month per number or user. Unlike tiered phone systems,


LinkedPhone


doesn’t offer multiple plans with different feature sets. You get the same core features with either option.


##


LinkedPhone pricing at a glance: What you get and what you’re missing


LinkedPhone is a virtual phone system that offers calling and texting. As a[second phone number app](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-second-phone-number-apps/) , it allows you to stay in touch with customers on the go as long as you have access to WiFi or data.


It also offers ticket management, letting you create tickets and assign them to teammates. It’s a good ‌business phone tool that keeps everything related to customer communication in one place. However, it might not be the right fit for growing small businesses that want to scale. As we dig into pricing and features, you’ll see why.


### **What you get with** **LinkedPhone**


**Here’s what you get when you sign up for** **LinkedPhone** **:**


**Pricing** **:** $19.99 per month for a local number or $29.99 per month for a toll-free number. Both local and toll-free plans include the same features and one user. Here’s a breakdown of the costs for[second phone numbers](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-second-phone-number/) and other features:

Also keep in mind: LinkedPhone limits you to 10 users during the initial seven-day free trial.


**Key features:**


- One user included
- Call forwarding and call transfer
- Number porting
- Business caller ID
- Voicemail
- Call recording

- Peer-to-peer messaging
- Available for iOS and Android
- AI call summaries
- Scheduled messages
- Auto-replies, including after-hours replies
- Group chats for up to five numbers
- Ring order and call routing
- Call menu greeting and options


### **What you’re missing with** **LinkedPhone**


LinkedPhone offers solid features for very small, local business owners who want to avoid[carrying two phones](https://www.quo.com/blog/carrying-two-phones/) . But it’s missing features that become vital as your business grows. For example, it doesn’t offer:


- A native desktop app so you can work from your computer
- HIPAA-compliant texting and calling
- International calling and texting outside the US and Canada
- Third-party integrations, aside from Zapier
- Advanced group texting
- Call analytics and reporting dashboards


##


LinkedPhone’s paid add-ons and other fees to know


LinkedPhone advertises “No locked features, no hidden fees, no surprises.” Is this really the case?


On the surface, yes, at least for single-user, single-number plans. However, you should be prepared to pay extra for:


- **Additional users and numbers.** LinkedPhone charges $5 per additional user and $5 per additional number. These costs can add up quickly for growing teams.


- **Premium AI features.** LinkedPhone’s sales pages cite “no locked features” and say that all plans include the same features. But their Terms of Service tell a slightly different story. They read, *“Certain Service features and usage levels carry additional fees, including additional team member seats, toll-free numbers… \[and\] premium AI features.”* It’s unclear what features are “premium AI features” or how much extra they cost.


- **Call and text overage fees.** LinkedPhone offers unlimited calling and messaging, but there are still usage limits. If your usage goes beyond what LinkedPhone considers “standard” or “acceptable” business use, you’ll be on the hook for overage fees. They don’t publicly list how much those fees are or what counts as “standard” use. However, their Acceptable Use Policy forbids at least the following:


- Auto-dialing, predictive dialing, or any other non-manual calling
- Operating bulk call-in numbers
- Sending bulk SMS blasts
- Allowing more than one individual to use a single user number


- **Free features may not stay free.** Although everything is included in one plan *for now* , that may not be the case in the future. The Terms of Service explicitly state, “ *Certain features of the Service are currently offered at no charge. We reserve the right to begin charging for any free feature in the future. If we do, we will give you advance notice before the fee takes effect, and you will need to pay the applicable fee to continue using that feature* .”


##


5 Key things to keep in mind before choosing LinkedPhone


So, who should use LinkedPhone — and who shouldn’t? Here are five key things to keep in mind before you look to LinkedPhone for an[alternate phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/alternate-phone-number/) for your business:


### **1. You can’t make international calls**


LinkedPhone doesn’t support outbound international calling or texting. You can receive calls from international numbers, but you may incur additional fees and taxes. You can’t place outbound calls or send texts to international numbers. If you have customers, leads, or vendors outside the US, you’ll need to maintain a separate business phone system to contact them. This can be a major headache as you scale.


### **2. No native integrations with your other tools**


LinkedPhone lets you connect with other tools through[Zapier](https://www.quo.com/integrations/zapier) but doesn’t offer native integrations. This adds an extra step and subscription to connect your phone system with tools like:


- CRMs like[HubSpot](https://www.quo.com/integrations/gong) ,[Jobber](https://www.quo.com/integrations/jobber) , and[Salesforce](https://www.quo.com/integrations/salesforce)
- AI tools like[Claude](https://www.quo.com/integrations/claude) or[ChatGPT](https://www.quo.com/integrations/chatgpt)
- Sales tools like[Clay](https://www.quo.com/integrations/clay) or[Gong](https://www.quo.com/integrations/gong)
- Customer booking and calendar tools


This means fewer automations, duplicate work, lost data, and more gaps in your system.


### **3. No HIPAA-compliant texting or calling**


LinkedPhone doesn’t support HIPAA compliance. So healthcare teams can’t communicate in a compliant manner using LinkedPhone.


### **4. “Unlimited” calling and texting comes with usage limits**


LinkedPhone advertises unlimited calling and messaging. However, it comes with set usage limits they don’t clearly outline. If you go beyond what LinkedPhone considers “standard” or “acceptable” business use, you may have to pay overage fees. LinkedPhone doesn’t publicly list the cost of these overage fees.


This can make it harder to predict costs as your business grows and your team makes more calls and sends more texts. It can also make it difficult to predict how much to use automations and auto-reply features. These could send more texts to leads and customers than a “single team user” might reasonably make in one day.


### **5. Customers cite issues with the mobile app and features**


Some users report issues with the mobile app and other mobile features — which is a big problem since that’s one of the platform’s major features. For example:


*“When it forwards the call out to your personal cell phone, it completely loses the call instead of keeping it with the* *auto attendant. There are multiple bugs when trying to use the software on a cell phone.”* — LinkedPhone user on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/linkedphone/reviews/linkedphone-review-9558327)


*“Caller ID simply does not function, even for numbers saved in the linked phone address book (specifically on the mobile app). Customer service told me to delete the app and download it again. I did that probably 10 times; it’d work for a couple \[of\] calls, then stop working.”* — LinkedPhone user on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/linkedphone/reviews/linkedphone-review-7640696)


Many[Apple App Store reviews](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/linkedphone-pro-business-line/id1304985788?see-all=reviews) also cite significant glitches and bugs, including:


- Not allowing users to answer a call
- Sending calls straight to voicemail during business hours
- Glitches where texts and calls don’t come through or drop midway through
- Being unable to type or edit text messages
- Saving contact names incorrectly

##


**FAQs**


**Does LinkedPhone have a free trial?**


Yes, LinkedPhone offers a one-week free trial and claims you can test every feature before paying. Keep in mind that you can only add up to 10 team members during the trial period.


**Does LinkedPhone require a contract?**


LinkedPhone doesn’t require contracts. They offer month-to-month business phone services you can cancel anytime.


**Is LinkedPhone HIPAA compliant?**


No, LinkedPhone isn’t HIPAA compliant. Healthcare teams can only use LinkedPhone for messages that don’t contain personal health information. Better yet, look for a[HIPAA-compliant VoIP](https://www.quo.com/blog/hipaa-compliant-voip/) phone system like Quo.


**Does LinkedPhone have hidden fees?**


LinkedPhone claims to have no hidden fees. However, additional fees may be charged for inbound international calls or texts. Overages or high usage, additional users or members, and “premium AI features” can also incur fees. LinkedPhone doesn’t clearly state what the premium AI features are or what these fees would cost.


**Can you make international calls with LinkedPhone?**


No, LinkedPhone doesn’t support making or sending outbound international calls or texts.[VoIP providers for international calls](https://www.quo.com/blog/voip-international-calls/) include Quo, Nextiva, or Dialpad.
